Senses.Explanation: The verdict “toil, yet no result” (勞而無功) is applied in Chan records to fruitless searching, speaking, contrivance, and failed responses. Zhantang Wenzhun answers “I do not understand” with “toil without result.” Another retained address warns that pursuing outside objects spends effort without result. Verses and addresses use the same four graphs where exertion is expressly followed by failure to accomplish; the phrase judges the outcome of the labor, not labor as such.

Senses.Explanation: Turn the light back and reflect is a recurrent demand to examine one's own understanding, and the records also use the phrase to expose a counterfeit built from shutting out sights and sounds. Guishan Lingyou tells Yangshan Huiji to turn the light back because nobody else knows Yangshan's understanding, and asks him to present that understanding. Yuanwu Keqin rebukes an audience that will not turn back despite being stopped at every sense gate; Tianyin Yuanxiu tells an assembly not to seek outside; Dahui Zonggao addresses officials absorbed in public business. Zhongfeng Mingben supplies the sharpest limit: he says people who withdraw sight and hearing until they resemble wood and stone falsely call that turning the light back. Jifei Ruyi instead pairs it with tracing the source of the delusive body, while Yuanwu's Essentials tells a student who has been turned by a phrase to turn back and inspect.

Senses.Note: Muzhou says he can spread out or draw together the matter at hand. A monk asks what he means by spreading it out, then refuses Muzhou’s offered phrases. Muzhou replies, “The cup falls to the ground; the saucer breaks into seven pieces.” Eryin calls this a seller meeting a blind buyer. Zhe’an says Muzhou’s ability cannot rescue the exchange once the monk tests him. Yezhu brings the cup line into a later sermon and repeatedly draws with his staff instead of relying on old words. Senses.Explanation: A refuse heap is a heap of discarded filth. The retained records use it literally as a place on or in which something may be smothered, buried, appear, or be found. An unnamed monk speaks of smothering Yunmen on its top; Zhenjing Kewen says several muddied people could be buried in it. Xuedou says a full-sized golden body appears there, and Dongshan Liangjie compares his joy to finding a bright pearl there during his dialogue with Yunyan Tansheng. The last two uses show that the heap’s low condition does not decide the value of what appears on it. The surviving evidence selected here comes through lamp and lineage compilations, so the article remains provisional.

Senses.Explanation: The top of a dung-sweepings heap is the refuse pile where discarded and filthy things collect. Chan masters repeatedly make it the unlikely place where a jewel, treasure, robe, shoe, or even a golden body is found, while also using the same heap for adding still more rubbish. Juelang Daosheng says the Buddha found a mud pellet on the heap and raised it before the assembly. Muting Pufu calls a display of pots, tiles, bamboo scraps, and bricks “adding more rubbish atop the dung heap.” Xuedou Chongxian places a sixteen-foot golden body on the heap before setting that proposition aside. Changling Zhuo’s verse says treasure is found there without seeking. Dongshan Liangjie compares joy after leaving holy truth undone to finding a bright pearl on the heap. Yehai Ziqing says he found a torn robe there and kept it for decades. Mi’an Xianjie uses the rubbish-adding frame after saying that even forgetting both delusion and awakening remains additional refuse.

Senses.Explanation: The point-and-never-arrive of the Chan records: the blocked road — the newcomer shouted down, the bamboo and peach-blossom awakenings ruled past pointing, the Shaolin message, the reunion without expedients, and the whisk-flick on say-and-don't-say. Xuedou Chongxian tests the six newcomers: any author-masters of Chan here? The leader: what does the abbot say? — Point and you don't arrive. The monk goes to deliberate — a shout. Silence. Dragon head, snake tail. The second, asked why he doesn't answer for the leader — one slap. The third, blank — one charge-sheet covers all, Hongzhi Zhengjue weighs the famous awakenings: everyone says Xiangyan struck the bamboo and his mind brightened, Lingyun saw the peach blossoms and woke — was it really so? At that time, arrive and it wasn't pointed; now, point and you don't arrive, Zhenjing Kewen takes the Shaolin-message ask — if it were so, the Shaolin tidings would be cut off, yet the traces stand plain — the monk bows — and he answers: point and you don't arrive; then his own address: the wonder of the way's teaching only returns to its source; returned to source, nothing is not allowed, all stands present, the ocean-seal giving light — now together with the assembly returned to source, dwelling in the equal basis: which is the source, which the wonder? — only because it was utterly plain, the attaining came late, and Linye Tongqi meets an old friend: formerly we met without talking Chan — today reunited, should I talk the way? Not that this mountain monk lacks expedients — only that in this matter pointing cannot arrive: propose it before the words and you're sealed in the shell; master it under the phrase and you run mad along every road. Only the out-of-rank spirit doesn't enter by either track — and the one line beyond delusion and waking? He remembers the third month of Jiangnan: where the partridge cries, a hundred flowers scent. Yikui Yuankui's evening address: lightning rolls, stars race — arrive and it isn't pointed; the moment thought stirs — point and you don't arrive. And once both ends are sat cut through, the one gate above split open: one line holding the three mysteries, one mystery holding the three essentials — what a gate! Examine it out and you're no false Shending guest of Chan; fail, and the Zhengzhou pear, the Qingzhou date — at bottom nothing beats a good provenance, Xieyun Jiji grades the Qinshan-Yantou brothers: they turned the grandfather's resounding family name into wind-flowers-snow-moon — striking in with his own verse: born on the same branch, their bearing differs; riding sound and covering color, what difference? Plucking the flower-branch for a wine-tally, playing wind and moon through rain and mist — point and you don't arrive: great skill seems clumsy — then the sudden staff: fallen red covers the ground with no one sweeping, all of it the traveler's eyes' blood, and Guantao Daqi's evening address: point and you don't arrive, arrive and you don't point — Huangmei's waist-dropping stone, moss-grown in wind and rain; master Touzi barefoot down to Tongcheng — what you are all used to seeing; the copper sieve brimming with oil — how do you tell the host from it? One monk bowed and walked straight out; the master: hearing the name is not like meeting the face.

Senses.Explanation: To inspect means to check a person, statement, or handling and, where it fails, call it to account. Pingtian Puan says his teacher would otherwise be exposed to inspection by masters elsewhere; Shanyang Anzhu fears being inspected for the reason he gives for staying on the mountain; and the head monk Ying describes an abbot as habitually inspecting others. Wansong Xingxiu, Xisou Shaotan, and Tianru Weize use the verb while weighing earlier masters' conduct or words. The object of inspection changes, but the ordinary transitive action remains the same.

Senses.Explanation: Even turning stone into gold or jade is easier than persuading people to put down right-and-wrong judgments. The comparison sets a marvel beside a persistent human habit. Yikui gives the line after testing an older master and strikes his staff. Linye offers it as a note to his assembly while gesturing with a whisk. Sanyi uses it after saying that both attachment to and rejection of appearances merit a blow. In these turns the difficulty is practical, not a claim about literal alchemy. Chaozong closes his own comment on a general asking to have killing washed away with the comparison. Hansong gives the comparison as his own reply after a monk compares sword and medicine.

Occurrences.Kwic: 乃云。在天成象在地成形。日月為照臨。四時作寒暑。居谷盈谷處坑滿坑。有情則動轉施為。無情則森羅顯煥。如今在山僧拄杖頭上。指山山崩。指海海竭。點鐵成金。點金成鐵。攪長河為酥酪。化酥酪為長河。見諸人不會。變作無邊

Senses.Explanation: The paired transformations describe Yuanwu’s unrestricted ability to elevate, overturn, and reverse valuations. Yuanwu lists them first as the function of Yuanwu’s staff and later as his own staff’s universal activity. The Blue Cliff pointer and Yuanwu’s sermon are distinct uses of the same reversible-transformation image.
